wrong_controls.name: WC1_linear_scaling_explicitly_rejected
wrong_controls.details: Linear scaling N * 1/16 grows without bound and violates the gravity channel ceiling identified in CR121.  Rejected as the SAM-native scaling law.

wrong_controls.name: WC2_parallel_sharing_explicitly_rejected
wrong_controls.details: Parallel-sharing constant 1/16 split N ways does NOT scale capacity -- it just dilutes the single-letter content.  Rejected as the SAM-native scaling law.

wrong_controls.name: WC3_geometric_subdivision_matches_closure_depth_ladder
wrong_controls.details: Letter N requires closure depth D+N.  This matches SAM's closure-depth ladder naturally: each successive letter is one deeper in the binary resolution structure.

wrong_controls.name: WC4_asymptotic_limit_NOT_full_unity
wrong_controls.details: The asymptotic limit is 2^-D = 1/8, NOT 1.  Paul Revere transmission is confined to the gravity-coupled subspace, which is the Higgs-released fraction.  Standard Born unity is NOT violated.

wrong_controls.name: WC5_q_0_only_scope
wrong_controls.details: CR067a is q = 0 specific per CR066a/CR066b.  Whether the geometric scaling extends to q >= 1 rows is a separate open question.

wrong_controls.name: WC6_practical_cutoffs_acknowledged
wrong_controls.details: Encoding deep-N letters requires high gate fidelity at closure depth D+N.  For practical NV implementations, N >= 8 may exceed achievable gate precision.  This is documented as an out-of-scope engineering question.

wrong_controls.name: WC7_falsifier_distinguishes_per_letter_vs_cumulative
wrong_controls.details: Three independent falsifiers: per-letter capacity differing from 2^-(D+N), cumulative exceeding 1/8, or saturating at a value different from 1/8.  Each tests a distinct claim of the geometric subdivision lock.
